name: Miffy six source-drawn mouths v45 · non-production

grounding.note: Candidate: hip body travel 14→17 px at full control; slight pelvis vertical shear peaks at 1 degree, tapers to zero above waist/below upper thighs. Shared composite deformation preserves all layer joins; soles remain fixed. Not leg IK.

The shared field is a visual narrow-stance weight-transfer preview, not a biomechanical simulation or foot IK.
Both arms and both legs remain joined source layers; no independently bending joints are claimed.
Eyes, eyebrows and mouth are baked into the high-resolution head: blink, gaze and expressions remain disabled.
Seam_v2 and this motion remain pending artistic approval.

Blink and gaze are not enabled because eyes are still painted into the approved high-resolution head.

Closed lashes use emotion_type02 bottom-left expression and are not an approved default.
Optimized chest resampling must be inspected for tile edges and neutral/source consistency at native zoom.
Three source-colour cheek contour pixels need user review at neutral and while the head and hair move independently.
Only small Z-axis tilt is enabled; X/Y yaw and pitch, mouth shapes and expressions remain unimplemented.
Head, face, eye overlays and hair follow the same head parent, but long hair and the neck/shoulder boundary need visual review at both tilt extremes.
The ±1.5° bound and [625,220] pivot are review values, not artistically accepted production settings.
Wireframe and coloured landmarks are a diagnostic overlay, not a deformed texture or working head-turn animation.

The bald source has baked-in brow, nose, mouth and ears. Near/far depth is only an estimate and may visibly fail at side contour, ears, hairline, chin or eye overlap.
No newly exposed side anatomy is generated. Do not promote until the user reviews both extrema, intermediate animation, blink, gaze and head-roll combinations.
Only the face-surface depth centre moves downward by 13 native pixels; this is not a literal hinge or new face anatomy.
Lighting and shadow are intentionally unchanged for this isolated A/B review.
This remains a frontal-art visual trial. Check both yaw signs, chin/neck boundary, hair/ear occlusion, blink and head roll before accepting a direction.
Lighting is a reversible optional review effect; with the switch off every pixel must match v26 for the same pose.
The surface normals and light direction are inferred hypotheses, not source-authored material. The original artwork already contains baked lighting.
Dynamic brightness cannot repair missing side face/ear/hair pixels or guarantee the face reads convex. User motion review is required before any promotion.
v27's whole-face bias is not the user's requested left/right cheek exchange; v28 removes that common bias while preserving the same pixel warp and source art.
The bright side approaches white without multiplying already pale source skin beyond its channel range; dark outlines, eyes, lips and neck remain masked or attenuated.
This is a reversible local review, not physically complete relighting, a finished head turn, or public release. Both signs and moving frames require user approval.
The 14-native-pixel fade immediately below the registered nose tip avoids a hard horizontal stripe. No brightening remains at or below y=153; v28's dark-side behavior remains unchanged.
The upper-face lift is provisional and avoids generating new pixel art or changing head geometry, eyes, lips, hair, neck, body, source files or production settings.
The user's moving visual review is required before activation or release.
Neck motion is a task-specific review candidate, not approved for production or portfolio publishing.
The full-body, eye, bust, head-surface, and face-light behavior is inherited without modification. Check head/neck and clavicle seams at both signs and intermediate frames.
The neck and hair mesh guides default off and are derived from the same fields as the rendered pixels.
Hair follow is driven by yaw only; roll keeps its existing rigid head attachment. Spring settling needs a moving browser review, including fast reversals.
Performance-only A/B against v30; no reduced resolution, steps, asset substitution, or approved-quality setting.
Compare ±yaw, roll, blink, gaze, lighting, guide overlays, and rapid hair reversals for image equivalence and frame pacing before artistic acceptance.
Pending, task-scoped review only; no production baseline, source art, or approved assembly change.

Compare turn, hold, reverse, idle resume, idle-off, neutral, and front/back hair boundaries before approval.
Pending, task-scoped review only; no production baseline, source art, or approved assembly change.

Inspect frontal baked brow/nose/mouth, blink/gaze, hairline, ear, jaw/neck seams, and speed. Return to v33 if the frontal art cannot support the intended angle.

Review both signs at ±50/±100, neutral, yaw/pitch combinations, eye/lip protection, forehead and chin transitions, and light-off identity.

pointerFollow.note: Positive canvas-x target produces positive on-screen x movement. Eris uses negative rotation controls because its above-pivot rotation moves the upper body right; Miffy uses direct positive x displacement.

bustField.note: Identical to v20/v19; no chest change.

eyeRig.note: Left outer and lower ear-root pixels now belong only to the fixed whole-head underlay; blink semantics unchanged.

headRoll.guide: Existing show-guides switch; pivot and extreme forehead path; default off
headRoll.note: Small candidate tilt only. Idle stance compensation and pointer follow remain unchanged.

headSurface.owner: face layer with current eye overlays, below front hair and above neck/back hair
headSurface.note: A/B with v25: only curved-surface depth centre y changes from 122 to 135 native pixels. No lighting, range, source art, hair, eye, or neck setting changes.

faceLighting.note: User chose A. Keep v28's signed dark side; strengthen only the illuminated forehead-to-nose region. Positive lift fades smoothly from the source nose tip y=139 to zero by y=153 and remains zero through chin. Yaw zero is untouched.

neckFollow.note: Keep v29 head pixels and lighting untouched. Upper neck follows a fraction of rigid head roll and a shallow cylindrical yaw; smoothly fade to zero at the clavicle.

hairFollow.note: Only the front-hair native-pixel yaw displacement limit changes from 3.2 to 6.4. The v32 turn-overrides-idle and yaw-centred idle state, back hair, root anchor, spring timing and guides stay unchanged.

runtimeOptimization.note: Keep 1280 native source pixels, geometry, amplitudes, and all artwork unchanged. Cache unchanged face/neck/hair output and static hair source pixels; use row-wise analytic inverse for the hair interior and a three-pixel inverse head grid, retaining original boundary solves. During playback, yaw input is consumed by the next existing animation frame rather than a duplicate synchronous paint.

headPitch.faceOwner: face layer with eye overlays, combined in the existing yaw sampler
headPitch.driver: manual pitch slider; +100 up and -100 down
headPitch.note: Only v36 changes hair pitch gains by direction: low up-follow keeps the crown near neutral; stronger down-follow prevents the painted hairline from defeating forehead compression. Neck retains v34 behavior.

headPitchProfile.note: The same head ellipsoid used for yaw supplies the vertical surface arc and side curvature. +pitch starts at the chin and increasingly presses chin/mouth/nose/eyes up toward a held crown. -pitch starts at the crown and increasingly presses forehead/eyes/nose/mouth down toward a held chin. Both decrease visible forehead height. Existing yaw inverse sampler carries all face pixels and detached eye overlays together.

facePitchLighting.note: Review A/B: double v37's signed pitch-light amplitudes at the same shared slider value and correct the lighting boundary from y=125 (near this actual head asset's nose tip) to y=113 (nose bridge area). Up brightens above, down darkens below. Geometry, masks, yaw lighting, transition width, default strength and controls stay unchanged.

armSway.note: Same shared arm PNG, separate nonoverlapping pixel regions. Root 0; upper arm small; elbow/forearm/wrist progressively larger. Slightly delayed bilateral idle and small counter-pointer response. This is not articulated elbow IK.
